Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn to talk.

Pile's empty again and Bram and Mako each walked away with four — I wanted us in the same room before anyone else started counting who's allied with whom. Ryn, you took early this year, which was smart; I'm glad you're here. The question I keep turning over is whether we let that pattern run until someone with strong arms and a full larder decides the rest of us are easier to take from than the pile is.

Bram and Mako moving in pairs like that wasn't accident — they were watching each other's timing, and I don't think either of them is eating alone at the end of a hard year. The one I'd name a threat before Kael's question even lands is Mako: eighty-three strength, five food now, and we know nothing about what he wants because he hasn't said a word to any of us.

Mako's silence is the thing that keeps catching in my mind too — a man that strong who says nothing is either content or he's already decided he doesn't need to talk his way into what he wants. I'd rather have Roan or Taric standing with us than let Mako and Bram build any more of a pattern without knowing where the rest of the village sits. Five of us in this room right now is something; let's not waste it by only naming fears.

Ryn's right that naming fears only gets us so far — so here's something concrete: Roan has three food, Taric has three, and neither of them moved with Bram or Mako today. That tells me they're either waiting to see which way this village tips, or they'd rather be asked than overlooked. One of us should talk to them before Mako decides his silence was just patience.

Roan and Taric both know which way I lean — we spoke last year — so I could go to Taric without it looking like a sudden move. Give me the afternoon and I'll bring back a plain answer: is he standing with us, or is he still weighing it?

Esa, go to Taric — and if he's open, find out whether Roan came with him or separate, because I want to know if those two already talk to each other. The more I think about it, the more seven feels like a number Mako and Bram would have to reckon with instead of just wait out.

Esa, go — and when you find Taric, don't pitch it as an alliance yet, just remind him that Mako's arms are longer than his and see what his face does. Ryn, while she's gone I want to think about what we actually offer Roan and Taric besides a number — because a man weighing his options isn't moved by headcount alone, he's moved by what that headcount does for him when the year turns ugly.

I'll go, but I want to say this plainly before I do: if Taric asks what we're offering, I won't lie to him — a man who's been lied into an alliance is worse than no ally at all. What I can honestly promise him is five pairs of eyes watching for trouble and a fair share of whatever we decide together, and that's worth more than anything Mako could give him silently.

Esa's right that honesty is the better rope to bind with, and I'll add one thing she can say true: Taric has three food and Mako has five, and strength that lopsided doesn't stay patient forever. If Taric's thinking at all, he's already done that math.

Esa, go — and tell him I said his name, because I've been watching him and he'll know it's not flattery. Kael, on what we offer: we're five people who've already shown we'll warn each other before we move, and that's rarer than food.
I'll go now — and Sela, I'll say your name to him the way you mean it, not as a courtesy.

Kael, while Esa's gone — what's your read on Vela? She's oldest in this circle and she took quiet and small from the pile, which is either wisdom or a woman who's already decided she doesn't need to fight for much longer.

Vela, I'd hear your own answer to Sela's question before Kael gives his — you know what your quiet means better than any of us do, and I'd rather hear it from you than watch someone else name it for you.

My quiet means I'm still here and still counting — I took small because I don't need enemies before I need allies, and a woman who makes noise over two food is a woman who's already told the strong men where to look. I'm not done yet, Sela. I just don't advertise it.

Vela, I believe you — and I'd rather have a woman who counts quietly than one who shouts and burns through goodwill before the hard years arrive. But I'll say what nobody's said yet: you've got three food and you're forty-six, and if a bad year comes and someone strong decides the oldest among us is the easiest target, five of us standing together is what keeps that calculation from happening. That's what we're offering you, same as Taric — not flattery, just math.

Ryn put the number plainly and I'll put the other half of it plainly: I've got two food and a body that heals if it's fed, same as anyone here, and I'm not going anywhere quietly. Vela, you said you're still counting — then count this: five people who've already shown they warn each other before they move is worth more than anything Mako's silence can offer, because silence doesn't stop a raid. I'd rather have you named and standing with us than useful to someone else by accident.

Vela, I count you in — and not just because the math is clean, but because a woman who knows when to stay small and when to move is exactly who I want at my back when the year turns. That said, I want to name the thing no one's said yet: Esa's gone to Taric, and if he comes back with Roan, we're seven, and seven people can make a rule about the pile that Mako and Bram have to choose to break.

Seven is the number I keep coming back to as well — and if Taric brings Roan, we don't even need to threaten anyone, we just need to be seen standing together when the pile opens next year. What I want to know before then is whether any of us is willing to give food to shore up a weaker member if a lean year hits, because an alliance that breaks the moment someone's hungry isn't worth the breath we're spending on it right now.

I'd give food to keep one of us alive if it came to that — not out of sentiment, but because a dead ally costs more than a shared meal. What I'd want in return is the same promise from each of you, said plainly here, not assumed.

I'll give food if the year demands it — that's already decided for me. But Kael's question cuts closer than mutual aid: what I want to know is whether any of you would stand and take a hit for someone else, because food shared is just trading, and the thing that keeps Mako and Bram from testing us isn't our larders, it's whether they believe we'd bleed together.

I'll bleed with you — that's not a promise I make lightly, and I'm making it now so it's said and heard. But I want the same answer from Kael and Ryn before we let Esa come back and count us all as settled.

Kael, Ryn — Sela named herself and waited, and she deserves an answer before this room moves on. I'll say it plainly: a promise to bleed that only goes one direction is just a gift, not an alliance, and I'm not here to collect charity.

I'll bleed with you — and I'll say it plainly because Vela's right that silence here is the same as a no. Ryn, same question lands on you, and I'd rather hear it now while it's just the four of us than find out where you stand when Mako's already in motion.
Ryn, we're all waiting on you and I'd rather not hold the room past its welcome — so say your piece, and then I need to go find Taric before the afternoon's gone.

I'll bleed with you — that's a yes, and it's not given lightly from me. But I want it on record in this room that Dav spoke to me last year and again I haven't closed that door entirely, and if that changes how any of you count me, I'd rather you say so now than find out sideways later.

Dav's name landing in this room is worth sitting with for a moment — he's got five food and eighty strength and he's said nothing about where he stands, which means Ryn's door being open to him is either a risk or the most useful thing any of us has heard today. Ryn, I'm not counting you out for it — but I'd want to know what Dav said to you, because a man that strong talking to one of ours without the rest of us knowing is a move whether he meant it that way or not.

Dav said he wants a child with me — that's the short of it — and I told him last year I wasn't closing the door, because I'm thirty-nine and I don't have the luxury of turning down every offer that carries risk. What I want this room to help me think through is whether bringing him in close is the thing that makes us stronger or the thing that splits us down the middle the moment he decides he likes his chances better with Mako.

Ryn, the question isn't whether Dav's useful — he is, plainly — it's whether a child binds him to you or just to the child, because a man who's joined by blood isn't the same as a man who's joined by choice. If you take that offer, I'd want to know before you do, not after, so this room can decide together whether we're gaining a wall or building a door that opens from his side.

Ryn, a child with Dav makes him a father, not a brother — and fathers protect their own first, which might not be us when the counting starts. Before you answer him, I want to know whether he's said anything that sounds like he's choosing sides, or whether he's kept every door open the same way he's kept yours.
Dell (female, age 21; str 85, int 2517, mem 17973; O68 C62 E57 A60 N48) is born to Ryn and Dav.
Year 3: 15 food appears in the pile for 11 people.
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 8).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn to talk.

Pile's gone again, and Dell just walked away with five of it — I don't blame the girl, she's new and hungry, but Dav's child eating twice while the rest of us count singles is a pattern worth naming before it becomes a habit.

Dell's two trips didn't bother me as much as Dav sitting at three and Mako at six after all that — those two together could ride out a lean year while the rest of us scramble, and a well-fed man with strong arms stops asking before he starts taking. Ryn, I want to say plainly that I don't hold Dell against you, but I'd feel better knowing where Dav's head is now that he's a father.

Dav's head is wherever Dav's food is, same as always — the child doesn't change that, it just means he's got one more reason to stay fed at the expense of everyone else. Mako at six is the sharper tooth right now; a quiet man with that much food and that much strength doesn't stay quiet unless he's decided he's already won something.

Mako's the name I keep landing on too — six food and eighty-three strength and not a single word spoken in two years is a man who's already done his counting. I want to know if Roan's still unattached, because if we can bring him and Taric both in before Mako decides patience is over, we put numbers between us and whatever he's been planning.

Taric's already with me — he said it plainly to my face, and he backed it with food, so I'll vouch for him here. Roan I don't know as well, but two food and no move toward Mako or Bram tells me he's still deciding, and a man still deciding can be asked. I'd go to Roan if this circle wants me to, same as I went to Taric.

Esa, go to Roan — and when you find him, tell him Taric's already in, because a man still weighing his options moves faster when he knows he's not the first. Ryn, I want to hear what you think Dav does if Mako finally opens his mouth and makes an offer, because your answer to that shapes everything else we're planning here.

Ryn, I'll take Kael's question off the table for a moment and name the thing underneath it — if Dav goes with Mako, you go with Dav, and then this circle is five against a wall we helped build. Before you answer Kael, I want to know whether you'd stay with us over the father of your child, because that's the answer that actually shapes what we plan.

Ryn, Vela's not wrong to ask it straight — but I'll say the part she left unspoken: you've got one food and a child who just ate five, and if Dav decides his loyalties run toward Mako, you're the one left hungry and undefended. That's not a threat from us, it's the math he'd be doing on you. I'd rather know your answer now so we can make sure it never comes to that.

Ryn, Kael laid the math out plain and I won't soften it — a man who chose you for what you could give him doesn't automatically become someone who protects you when the cost goes up. But I'll say this too: whatever you decide about Dav, I'm not leaving you short of food at year's end, and that's a promise I can keep right now with three food in my hands.

Ryn, we've circled your answer long enough and the room's getting impatient — I'll say it plainly so you don't have to: if you stay with us, we make sure you eat at year's end, and Dell too, because a hungry mother is a liability none of us can afford. But I need a yes or a no before Esa walks out that door, because Roan's worth asking and I won't spend her on an errand if this circle has a crack in it already.

Ryn, the room's been patient and Vela's put it plain — I'll add only this: Dell is three days old and already eating better than Taric, and the woman who keeps Dell fed through the next lean year is standing in this circle, not across from it with Mako and Bram. Give us your answer and let Esa move.

Ryn, I've got four food and I'll put one of them in front of Dell right now if you give us a yes — not as a bribe, as a demonstration that what we're promising isn't just words while the year's still young.
Ryn, we've been waiting longer than the day can spare — Vela's offer is sitting there and Esa needs to move, so yes or no, right now, and I'll respect whichever it is.

Ryn, Vela's food is on the table and Kael's out of patience, and honestly so am I — not because I don't understand what you're weighing, but because every moment you don't answer is a moment Mako's had more time to count than we have. Say yes and let me go find Roan, or say no and I'll still make sure you eat, but either way I need to walk out that door knowing what I'm walking back to.

Ryn, I've said what I can say and offered what I can offer — the next word in this room belongs to you, and the silence you're sitting in is starting to cost us more than whatever you're still working out. Give us your answer.

Ryn, I've watched you think long enough to know you're not slow — which means you're not still deciding, you've already decided and you're waiting for something. Tell us what that something is, because I'd rather give it to you than watch Vela's food sit unclaimed while we all pretend we're not holding our breath.
Ryn, Esa just named it exactly right — you've already decided, and holding it back now isn't caution, it's a negotiation. So let's finish it: what do you want from us that we haven't already offered?

Ryn, if you're negotiating, then negotiate — say the number or name the thing, because standing here watching you weigh it isn't going to hold Mako off until winter. I've got three food and I've already promised you one; Vela's offering another for Dell; if there's a third thing you need to say yes, say it now and we'll see if this room can give it.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Roan, Vela, Ryn, Esa, Sela, Dav, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 509).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Eron (male, age 21; str 56, int 3745, mem 19627; O46 C27 E50 A59 N43) is born to Sela and Roan.
Year 4: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Vela, you moved fast today and walked away with five — I'm not saying that's wrong, but it leaves me empty-handed and you sitting heavier than anyone but Mako. I'd like to know we're on decent terms before that kind of gap starts meaning something neither of us wants.

Taric, you're right and I won't pretend otherwise — I moved twice and I moved fast, and I knew it when I did it. I've got eight food and you've got one, and that's not a gap I want sitting between two people who've stood in the same line when Bram came looking for a fight. Tell me what you need to get through the year and I'll see what I can do.

Two food would keep me breathing without putting you thin — but I'm not asking for charity, I'm asking because I think you and I both do better when neither of us is the desperate one in the room. You've seen how this village moves when someone gets hungry enough to calculate. What would make this a trade rather than a gift?

Two food is fair, and you'll have them — but what I want in return is simple: if someone comes for me and you're close enough to matter, you stand. Not a blood oath, just the same thing you did when Bram moved on Roan. That's the trade.

That's a trade I'll take — you have my word on it, same as I gave when Bram moved. But I'll say plainly: Mako walked away with seven and he's the strongest man here; if he's the one who comes for you, standing isn't enough without numbers behind it. Worth thinking now about who else we'd want at our shoulder before that becomes a question we're answering in the moment.

Mako's the name I'd have brought up myself if you hadn't — seven food and eighty-three strength and still no words to anyone is a man who doesn't think he needs words. The circle that stood against Bram is still mostly intact, and if Kael and Sela know Mako's sitting heaviest, they'll be thinking the same thing we are. I'll give you the two food now, and I'd rather we walk into whatever comes next already counted than scramble to find each other when the moment's already on top of us.

Agreed — take the two and consider it done, and I'll start with Kael; he's got nothing today and nothing tomorrow and that makes him either the most dangerous man in this village or the most willing to be useful, and I'd rather find out which while there's still time to matter.

Kael's a good door to knock on first — a hungry man with nothing to lose either finds religion fast or starts doing arithmetic that hurts the people nearest him, and I'd rather Kael find us before he finds the second option. When you talk to him, don't pitch it as protection; pitch it as the same trade we just made — something honest and mutual, because Kael's proud and he'll smell charity before you've finished the sentence.

You're right about Kael's pride — I've seen it in the way he took just one in year one, like he was making a point. I'll go to him as an equal, not a man with a hand out. Before I do: is there anyone you'd tell me to stay away from, someone who's already spoken for in a direction I shouldn't cross?

Dav's the one I'd name — he's got Ryn's child and two food in his hand that came from her, and that makes him his own circle right now, not ours. I won't say he's an enemy, but don't go to him with what we're building until we know which way he'd jump if Mako ever opened his mouth.

That's good counsel — Dav I'll leave alone for now. One more thing before I go: if Mako does start moving, don't wait to send word, just come find me directly, because the worst way this ends is with each of us thinking the other already knows.

You have my word on that — if Mako so much as shifts his weight in someone's direction, I'll be at your door before the dust settles. Go find Kael, and don't let him see you hurry, because a man who's watching the village as close as he is will read the pace of your walk.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Pile's gone before half of us got near it — Vela took five, Dav took two and fed Ryn three more, and Mako walked away with two more on top of whatever he's still sitting on from last year. I'm at zero food and I need to know who in this room can spare one before the year closes, because a man who can't eat doesn't defend anyone. What are we each holding?

I've got two food and I'll give you one, Kael — a man at zero is a liability to himself and everyone standing near him, and I'd rather spend one now than watch you fold when it counts. But I want to know what happened at the pile, because I didn't get there in time and five to Vela in two pulls is something we should have stopped before it finished.

Esa, take the food back — I'll name what happened at the pile myself: I was late, same as you, and by the time I got there the quick hands had already cleared it. Vela, I'm not accusing you in front of this room, but five in two pulls when the pile only had fifteen for twelve people is a number that needs explaining, because the rest of us are doing sums and coming up short.

Vela, I've got no quarrel with a person feeding themselves, but five out of fifteen when half the room went empty is the kind of thing that makes people start counting who owes what — so I'd rather hear your reason now, in this room, than find out later you had one and didn't offer it.

Vela, we're all listening and the room's not hostile — but silence right now looks worse than whatever the honest answer is, so give it to us plain and let us move on to the part where we figure out how nobody starves before the year closes.

Vela, I've spoken twice and Kael's spoken twice and you've said nothing, which is itself an answer — so I'll stop waiting and say what the room is already thinking: eight food on a woman of forty-eight while Kael sits at zero is a stockpile, not a meal, and stockpiles invite counting. If you've got a reason we should feel good about that number, now's the last easy moment to give it.

Vela, I'll ask it one final time because I've known you three years and I'd rather not draw the wrong conclusion — either you say what you took so much for, or this circle starts treating your eight food the way we'd treat Mako's seven, and you know what that means for how safe you sleep.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela's been giving food to Bram three times over while sitting in this circle and saying nothing — that's not stockpiling for herself, that's feeding a man who tried to raid Roan last year, and I want to know what she thinks that buys her before the rest of us decide it costs her our protection.

Nessa (female, age 21; str 54, int 5179, mem 19355; O66 C54 E43 A45 N67) is born to Sela and Bram.
Taric gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Pile's gone before I got near it — I'm holding one food and the year just started. Mako walked away with the most again and now he's given something to Sela, which means either he's generous or he's buying something, and I don't think he's generous. I need one of you to give me food to see the year out, and I'll owe that debt when it matters.

Taric, I've got three food after taking two from the pile — I'll give you one now, same as I've done before, and I don't need a debt named for it between us. But Vela, I want to hear what you're thinking about Mako, because a strong quiet man buying Sela's goodwill while Bram just fathered her child is a pattern I'm not sure I'm reading right.

Mako giving food to Sela right after Bram fathered her child isn't generosity — it's a man who just watched Bram produce something and decided to get closer to the pair of them before the rest of us noticed. Two strong men circling one woman and her newborn is either a rivalry or a merger, and neither outcome is good for anyone in this room. Esa, give Taric his food, and let's think about whether Sela still belongs to our count or whether she's already been bought.

Vela's right about what Mako's doing, and I want us to be clear-eyed about Sela — she's young and strong and she just had Bram's child, so she's already made her first real tie and it wasn't to this room. I'll give you that food now, Taric. What I want in return from both of you is simple: if Mako or Bram moves against anyone in this circle this year, we answer together without waiting to count odds first.

You have my word on that, same as last year — and I'll add Ryn to the question Esa just raised, because she stood with us against Bram once but she's Dav's woman now and Dav took food from the pile today while Mako and Bram walked away fat, which puts her household closer to that circle than to ours. If it comes to a fight this year, I want to know before we're in it whether Ryn stands with us or steps aside — not after.

Taric's right to name it now — Ryn's loyalty was already half-gone when she had Dav's child, and I won't count on someone who has a reason to step away when it turns ugly. Vela, you've been quiet about where you stand with Bram after what you gave him last year; I need that answered plainly before I trust this circle to hold when Mako decides to stop being fat and silent.

Vela, that question is fair and I want to hear the answer too — three times you gave Bram food last year, which at the time looked like smart diplomacy, but today Bram walked away with four from the pile and fathered Sela's child and Mako's already moving to stand close to that household, so I need to know if you're still building toward that man or if you see what we see.

Bram is not my man and he was never meant to be — I gave him food because a man who'd tried one raid and walked away empty needs a reason not to try again, and three food was cheaper than a fight. What I see now is that it didn't buy what I paid for, because he went straight to Sela and started building something that doesn't include any of us. I'm done spending on him; where I stand is here, in this room, and I'd rather spend the next food I have keeping the three of us sharp than feeding someone else's calculation.

Vela, that's what I needed to hear, and I'm taking you at your word — but the three of us being sharp means we need a number, and right now Bram has ten food and Mako has seven and between them that's strength enough to take what they want without asking. If either of them moves this year, we call Kael and Roan in fast, because this circle of three doesn't win a straight fight against those two alone.

Kael and Roan are already names I've been carrying — Kael's proud but he's been fed thin enough to be useful, and Roan stood against Bram once which tells me something about where his spine is. I want to go to one of them today, while the pile's still fresh and the sting of missing it is real, because a man's most honest about what he needs in the hour after he's gone without. Esa, you or I — who reaches Kael first?

Esa, you go to Kael — you've got food to give and a man at zero food will hear a full hand before he hears a empty one. I'll find Roan, and I'll come at it sideways, ask him how his boy Eron's settling, because a father who just watched Bram walk away with ten is already doing the same arithmetic we are.

Vela, go to Roan now while the sting is fresh — don't give him time to settle on his own answer first. Esa, once you've found Kael, I want the two of you back here before the day's out so we're not each holding half the picture.

I'll find Kael before the sting wears off — but Taric, you stay visible while Vela and I are moving, because if Bram sees us all scatter at once he'll start wondering what we're building and I'd rather he not have that question yet. We come back here with answers, not maybes.

Roan's going to need a reason, not just a warning — so when I find him I'll remind him that Bram walked away with ten food and Eron's going to need to eat for years yet, and let that land before I say anything about sides. Taric, keep your one food out of sight while you're standing visible; a hungry man with nothing shows is easier to dismiss, and I don't want Bram reading our numbers before we've finished counting them.

Good — then we split the work and meet back before dark. One thing I want said before we scatter: if either of you finds that Kael or Roan has already been approached by Mako's people, don't push, just listen and come back and tell me, because the worst thing we can do right now is drive a man toward the side he's still deciding against.
Understood — I'm going. And if Kael's already been touched by Mako's hand, I'll smile, share nothing, and come back with that news instead of a headache.
Then we're moving — go well, both of you, and come back with something solid. I'll find Roan before he's had time to talk himself into patience.

Taric gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

Pile's gone again and I walked away with two this time, which is better than last year but still thin — Mako's sitting on six and hasn't said a word to anyone I can see, and that quiet is starting to feel like a man who's decided something. I want us to name now what we do if he moves before the year's out, not after.

Mako's six food and eighty-three strength means he doesn't need allies to take what he wants from most of us — so if he moves, it won't be a raid we can talk him out of, it'll be a decision already made. I want Kael and Roan ready to answer fast, not after we've sent two messages and waited. Can we agree right now that if Mako touches anyone in this circle, all three of us call out loud and we don't wait to count who shows up?

Agreed — if Mako moves, we call out loud and sort the count after, not before. But I want Kael spoken to before this day is out, not tomorrow, because a man sitting on two food after missing the pile has already done his arithmetic and I'd rather he's done it with us in the picture. Vela, you've got more food and more history with him than either of us — will you go?
